title: Graphing Other Trigonometric Functions
presenterNotes: Emphasize that tangent and cotangent have period $\pi$, not $2\pi$. This is a common point of confusion.
For secant and cosecant, students must understand the reciprocal relationship. Spend time showing how the graphs relate to cosine and sine.
The asymptotes are critical. Always find them first before sketching the branches.
The Blueprint block ties the section together. Use it to demonstrate a complete graphing process for each type of function.

confusionCorner.body: A common mistake is thinking all trig functions have period $2\pi$. Tangent and cotangent have [[imp:period $\pi$]]. Their graphs repeat twice as often as sine and cosine.
confusionCorner.title: Period of Tangent Is $\pi$, Not $2\pi$

explanation: The parent function $y = \tan x = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}$ has vertical asymptotes where $\cos x = 0$, i.e., at odd multiples of $\frac{\pi}{2}$.
The period of $\tan x$ is $\pi$ (not $2\pi$). The graph repeats every $\pi$ units.
The parent function $y = \cot x = \frac{\cos x}{\sin x}$ has vertical asymptotes where $\sin x = 0$, i.e., at multiples of $\pi$.
The period of $\cot x$ is also $\pi$.
Both functions have range all real numbers, no amplitude, and no maximum or minimum values.

formulaCard.formula: $$ \tan x = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x} \quad \cot x = \frac{\cos x}{\sin x} $$

questions.feedbackIfWrong: Asymptotes are at $\frac{\pi}{2} + n\pi$, which are odd multiples of $\frac{\pi}{2}$.

discoveryHook.scenario: Unlike the smooth hills of sine and cosine, tangent and cotangent graphs leap to infinity and repeat in a shorter cycle. They model ratios that change rapidly—like the slope of a line or the angle of a searchlight.

blocks.title: Characteristics of Tangent and Cotangent

formulaCard.formula: $$ y = a \tan bx $$ $$ \text{Period} = \frac{\pi}{|b|}, \quad \text{Asymptotes: } x = \pm \frac{\pi}{2|b|} \text{ (center cycle at 0)} $$

visuals.title: Key Values for $y = a \tan bx$ (one cycle, $a>0, b>0$)

explanation: The general form of a tangent function is $g(x) = a \tan bx$.
The period is $\frac{\pi}{|b|}$. The vertical asymptotes are at odd multiples of $\frac{\pi}{2|b|}$.
The parameter $a$ vertically stretches ($|a| > 1$) or shrinks ($0 < |a| < 1$) the graph.
The $x$-intercept remains at $0$ (for no horizontal shift). The halfway points are at $\left( \frac{\pi}{4b}, a \right)$ and $\left( -\frac{\pi}{4b}, -a \right)$.
If $a < 0$, the graph is reflected across the $x$-axis.

teacherCues: Write $g(x) = 2\tan 3x$. Ask: How do $a$ and $b$ affect the graph of the parent tangent function?
Show that the period is $\frac{\pi}{|b|}$ and the asymptotes shift to $x = \pm \frac{\pi}{2|b|}$.

discoveryHook.scenario: Just like stretching a rubber sheet, the parameters $a$ and $b$ stretch or shrink the tangent graph vertically and horizontally. The asymptotes move too, creating steeper or shallower branches.

confusionCorner.title: Period Formula for Tangent
confusionCorner.body: For tangent and cotangent, the period is $\frac{\pi}{|b|}$, [[imp:not]] $\frac{2\pi}{|b|}$. Only sine, cosine, secant, and cosecant have period $\frac{2\pi}{|b|}$.

confusionCorner.title: Cotangent Starts at an Asymptote
confusionCorner.body: Unlike tangent (which passes through the origin), a standard cotangent cycle begins at a vertical asymptote $x=0$. The graph then decreases toward the next asymptote. [[imp:Don't confuse the intercept location with tangent.]]

visuals.title: Key Values for $y = a \cot bx$ (one cycle, $a>0, b>0$)

explanation: The general form is $g(x) = a \cot bx$. The period is $\frac{\pi}{|b|}$.
The vertical asymptotes for $y = a \cot bx$ are at multiples of $\frac{\pi}{|b|}$ (i.e., $x = 0$, $\pm \frac{\pi}{b}$, $\pm \frac{2\pi}{b}$, …).
The $x$-intercept is at $x = \frac{\pi}{2b}$ (halfway between asymptotes).
Halfway points: $\left( \frac{\pi}{4b}, a \right)$ and $\left( \frac{3\pi}{4b}, -a \right)$.
Cotangent decreases from left to right (for $a>0$).

discoveryHook.scenario: Cotangent graphs look like flipped and shifted tangent graphs. By stretching the period, we can model slowly changing ratios—like the angle of a camera panning up a building.

formulaCard.formula: $$ \sec x = \frac{1}{\cos x}, \quad \csc x = \frac{1}{\sin x} $$ $$ \text{Graph the reciprocal, then sketch secant/cosecant using asymptotes.} $$

legend.meaning: touches cosine at its peaks and valleys
touches sine at its peaks and valleys

visuals.title: Secant and Cosecant from Sine and Cosine

explanation: To graph $y = a \sec bx$, first graph the cosine function $y = a \cos bx$. Draw vertical asymptotes where $\cos bx = 0$.
The secant graph has branches touching the cosine graph at its maximum and minimum points, and curving away near the asymptotes.
Similarly, to graph $y = a \csc bx$, first graph $y = a \sin bx$, and draw asymptotes where $\sin bx = 0$.
The period for secant and cosecant is $\frac{2\pi}{|b|}$ (same as sine and cosine).
The range is $(-\infty, -|a|] \cup [|a|, \infty)$. There is no amplitude.

steps: Plot points where secant touches cosine: $(0,2)$ (max of cosine), $(\pi,-2)$ (min of cosine).
Sketch secant branches approaching asymptotes from these points.

steps: Plot points where cosecant touches sine: $(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{2})$ (max), $(\frac{3}{2}, -\frac{1}{2})$ (min).

confusionCorner.body: The range of $y = a\sec x$ and $y = a\csc x$ is $(-\infty, -|a|] \cup [|a|, \infty)$. The graph has a 'gap' between $-|a|$ and $|a|$. [[imp:There are no $y$-values in that gap.]]

discoveryHook.scenario: Secant and cosecant are the reciprocals of cosine and sine. Their graphs borrow the waves of sine and cosine, but shoot to infinity wherever the original function is zero—creating dramatic branches and valleys.

blocks.title: Blueprint Aid — Graphing Other Trigonometric Functions

explanation: [[imp:Understand]]: Determine the type of function (tan, cot, sec, csc). For sec/csc, identify the reciprocal cosine/sine function. Note the values of $a$ and $b$ to find period and asymptotes.

[[imp:Solve]]: 1. For tan/cot: mark asymptotes, $x$-intercept, and halfway points using formulas involving $\frac{\pi}{b}$. 2. For sec/csc: graph the reciprocal function ($a\cos bx$ or $a\sin bx$) lightly; draw asymptotes where that function crosses the $x$-axis; plot points where sec/csc touch the reciprocal at its peaks/valleys; sketch branches.
[[imp:Conclude]]: State the period, asymptotes, domain, and range. Label key points. Verify with a calculator or table.

confusionCorner.title: Secant/Cosecant: Don't Forget the Gap
confusionCorner.body: After graphing secant or cosecant, remember there are no $y$-values between $-|a|$ and $|a|$. The graph never enters that horizontal band. [[imp:This is the most common graphing mistake.]]

discoveryHook.scenario: When a tangent, cotangent, secant, or cosecant function has multiple transformations, the Blueprint keeps you organized: identify the type, use its reciprocal if needed, find period and asymptotes, and sketch.
